newsitem.title: USA: ADM shares rise on Justice settlement.
newsitem.headline: ADM shares rise on Justice settlement.

text.p: Shares of Archer Daniels Midland Co rose 3/4 to a new 52-week high of 21-3/8 after the company announced a $100 million plea agreement settlement with the U.S. Justice Department resolving an antitrust investigation.
"The stock is up because you now have a quantifiable amount (of fines pending against ADM)," Piper Jaffray analyst George Dahlman said. "And you've got a favorable commodity environment."
ADM's shares, which had been hovering between $17 and $19 a share for much of the year, have been rising in recent weeks due to lower corn prices that improve its grain processing margins.

Earlier, ADM said it agreed to enter into a plea agreement with the Justice Department and will plead guilty to two counts of anticompetitive conduct. As part of the plea, ADM will pay a $70 million fine for lysine, a feed additive, and a $30 million fine in connection with citric acid, a food and beverage additive.
ADM said the agreement resolves the Justice Department's investigation against it, including a probe of high-fructose corn syrup pricing practices.
